quotes.text: The difference between fast and real-time is about the relationship between data and action, not speed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes real-time analytics around action instead of refresh speed.

quotes.text: Instead of data flowing into a database and waiting for someone to ask a question, data flows into a system that's already listening, watching and ready to respond.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A vivid description of how streaming systems differ from stored-data analytics.

quotes.text: Real-time dashboards are for operational monitoring, seeing what's happening right now. Power BI is for deeper analysis over time, they serve different purposes, and you can use both.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies when to use real-time dashboards versus Power BI.

quotes.text: If you can describe the action you take with the data and that action needs to happen within seconds, real-time is for you. If you're just curious to see the number sooner, it's probably not.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple rule of thumb for deciding whether real-time is worth the cost.

quotes.text: The most common mistake is thinking you need real-time when you actually just need faster batch processing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns against building expensive streaming systems that are not needed.

chapters.title: Real-time is not just faster dashboards
The shift from batch to streaming
When you need it and how it connects

takeaways: Real-time intelligence is about shortening the time between signal and action, not about refreshing reports faster.
Its four building blocks are eventstreams for ingestion, Eventhouse for storage and KQL queries, real-time dashboards for live views and Activator for automated action.
Use real-time only when action must happen within seconds and combine it with OneLake and batch analytics for historical, cost-efficient analysis.
hook: Many teams confuse real-time intelligence with faster Power BI refreshes and either overbuild or miss critical signals. This episode explains for data and analytics professionals what Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence really is, how its four building blocks work, and when streaming is actually worth it.
